title: Why Doesn't Your Stomach Digest Itself?
short_title: Why Doesn't Your Stomach Digest Itself?
description_short:
Why doesn't your stomach digest itself? Its inner lining produces a protective layer of mucus. That barrier helps shield the stomach wall from its own digestive juices, while food gets mixed and broken down.

This is a simplified illustration: the mucus barrier is one part of the stomach's protection, not the full list of its defenses, and the animation is not real medical imagery.

Sources:
Cleveland Clinic, Stomach: https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/body/21758-stomach
Cleveland Clinic, Mucosa: https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/body/23930-mucosa
